# Branching Ratios of $B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta^{(\prime)}$ Decays in the Perturbative QCD Approach

## Motivation

This study is motivated by the recent experimental measurement of the branching ratio of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta$ decay. The availability of this first experimental result provides a valuable opportunity to confront theoretical predictions with data, thereby offering new insights into the underlying dynamics governing these processes.

## Theoretical Framework and Calculations

In this work, the researchers calculate the branching ratios of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta$ and $B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'$ decays using the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach. This framework enables a systematic treatment of the relevant hadronic matrix elements and provides a consistent theoretical basis for predicting the decay rates of these channels.

## Results

The pQCD prediction for the branching ratio of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta$ decay is
$$
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta) = (1.96^{+9.68}_{-0.65}) \times 10^{-6}.
$$
This value is consistent, within the quoted uncertainties, with the first experimental measurement of this channel, lending support to the applicability of the pQCD approach for describing such decays.

In parallel, the predicted branching ratio for the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta'$ decay is
$$
BR(B_d^0 \to J/\psi \eta') = (1.09^{+3.76}_{-0.25}) \times 10^{-6}.
$$
This result is of a magnitude similar to that of the $\eta$ channel, and it lies within a range that should be accessible to and testable by forthcoming LHC experiments.

## Implications

Measurements of these decay channels can play an important role in clarifying the QCD dynamics operating at the corresponding energy scale. Furthermore, such measurements provide a means to assess the reliability of the pQCD approach when applied to these B meson decays, thereby helping to establish the validity and limitations of the theoretical framework in this sector.

# Branching Ratios of $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta$ and $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'$ Decays in the pQCD Approach

## Introduction and Motivation

The study of $B$ meson decays into charmonium final states provides a valuable testing ground for our understanding of the strong interaction dynamics that govern heavy-flavor physics. In particular, decays of the type $B \to J/\psi + P$, where $P$ denotes a light pseudoscalar meson, are of considerable theoretical and experimental interest because they combine the presence of a heavy $c\bar{c}$ bound state with the rich phenomenology of light-meson production. Recently, an experimental measurement of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta$ channel has become available, motivating a renewed theoretical effort to compute the corresponding branching ratios and to confront these predictions with the data.

The $\eta$ and $\eta'$ mesons are especially interesting final-state particles because of the well-known $\eta$–$\eta'$ mixing, which links their quark-flavor content to the underlying structure of the light-quark sector. As a result, decays involving these mesons offer a sensitive probe not only of the decay dynamics but also of the mixing parameters and the possible gluonic content of the $\eta'$.

## Theoretical Framework

In this work, we adopt the perturbative QCD (pQCD) approach based on $k_T$ factorization to calculate the branching ratios of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta$ and $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'$ decays. The pQCD framework incorporates the transverse momentum of the valence quarks and employs the Sudakov resummation to suppress the contributions from the non-perturbative endpoint regions, thereby rendering the perturbative calculation of the relevant hard-scattering amplitudes reliable and self-consistent. Within this formalism, the decay amplitudes are expressed as convolutions of the process-dependent hard kernels with the universal, non-perturbative meson distribution amplitudes.

The calculation accounts for the $\eta$–$\eta'$ mixing in the quark-flavor basis, allowing a consistent treatment of the two final states. The relevant hadronic inputs, including the decay constants and distribution amplitudes of the $B_d^0$, $J/\psi$, and light pseudoscalar mesons, are taken from established determinations, and the effective weak Hamiltonian is used to describe the underlying quark-level transitions.

## Results and Discussion

Our numerical predictions yield branching ratios of approximately

$$
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta) \approx 1.96 \times 10^{-6},
$$

$$
\mathcal{B}(B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta') \approx 1.09 \times 10^{-6}.
$$

The predicted branching ratio for the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta$ channel is found to be in good agreement with the currently available experimental measurement, providing an important confirmation of the pQCD approach in this class of decays. The prediction for the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'$ channel, while not yet measured, lies at a level that is well within the reach of ongoing and forthcoming experiments.

Both branching ratios are of order $10^{-6}$, making them accessible to the high-luminosity data samples being accumulated at the LHC. In particular, the upcoming LHC experiments are expected to be able to measure or further constrain these channels, thereby offering a direct test of our theoretical predictions.

## Conclusion

By calculating the branching ratios of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta$ and $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta'$ decays within the pQCD approach, this study provides theoretical predictions that can be directly compared with experiment. The consistency of the $B_d^0 \to J/\psi\,\eta$ result with the recent measurement, together with the testability of both channels at the LHC, reinforces confidence in the reliability of the pQCD approach for describing these $B$ meson decays. Future experimental measurements of the $\eta'$ channel will further sharpen this comparison and deepen our understanding of the interplay between charmonium production and light-meson dynamics in heavy-flavor physics.

# Understanding the J/ψ Particle Through the Lens of QCD

## Introduction

The study of subatomic particles has long been **motivated** by our desire to understand the fundamental forces that govern the universe. Among the many discoveries in particle physics, the **J/ψ** (J/psi) meson holds a special place, serving as a crucial testing ground for **Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD)**—the theory describing the strong nuclear force.

## The Discovery of the J/ψ Particle

The J/ψ particle was independently discovered in November 1974 by two research teams, an event so significant it became known as the "November Revolution" in particle physics. This meson is composed of a charm quark bound to its antiquark counterpart, making it the first observed example of "charmonium." Its unexpectedly long lifetime and narrow decay width were features that physicists were strongly **motivated** to explain.

## The Role of QCD

**QCD** provides the theoretical framework for understanding how quarks and gluons interact through the strong force. The behavior of the J/ψ particle offered valuable insights into several key aspects of the theory:

- **Asymptotic freedom**: At short distances, the strong force becomes weaker, allowing quarks to behave almost freely.
- **Color confinement**: Quarks cannot be isolated individually, remaining perpetually bound within composite particles.
- **The OZI rule**: This principle helps explain the suppressed decay rates that give the **Psi** particle its characteristically narrow width.

## Why the J/ψ Remains Important

Researchers continue to be **motivated** to study the J/ψ because it acts as a "clean" system for probing **QCD** predictions. Because the charm quark is relatively heavy, theoretical calculations become more tractable, allowing physicists to compare experimental results with computational models with greater precision.

## Conclusion

The interplay between the **J/ψ** particle and **QCD** exemplifies how a single discovery can reshape an entire field. **Motivated** by curiosity and the pursuit of deeper understanding, physicists have used this remarkable particle to validate and refine our knowledge of the strong force, cementing its legacy as a cornerstone of modern particle physics.

# Abstract

Recent measurements of charmless hadronic $B$-meson decays by the LHCb and Belle II collaborations have revealed intriguing tensions with Standard Model expectations, most notably in the branching ratio of the $B \to \pi K$ system, which continues to challenge our understanding of the interplay between tree-level and penguin amplitudes in the heavy-quark sector. Motivated by the latest measurement of $\mathcal{B}(B^0 \to \pi^+ K^-) = (1.98 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{-5}$, which exhibits a persistent deviation from theoretical predictions, we investigate two related decay channels within the framework of perturbative QCD (pQCD) based on the $k_T$ factorization approach. Employing next-to-leading-order Wilson coefficients and incorporating threshold and transverse-momentum resummation effects, we compute the branching ratios and CP-violating asymmetries for the $B^0 \to \pi^+ K^-$ and $B^+ \to \pi^0 K^+$ decays. Our numerical results yield $\mathcal{B}(B^0 \to \pi^+ K^-) = (1.85^{+0.42}_{-0.35}) \times 10^{-5}$ and $\mathcal{B}(B^+ \to \pi^0 K^+) = (1.24^{+0.31}_{-0.26}) \times 10^{-5}$, in reasonable agreement with the experimental data within theoretical uncertainties. Furthermore, we find the direct CP asymmetries $A_{CP}(B^0 \to \pi^+ K^-) = -0.098 \pm 0.021$ and $A_{CP}(B^+ \to \pi^0 K^+) = +0.043 \pm 0.015$, whose difference sheds light on the long-standing "$\pi K$ puzzle." These predictions provide a stringent test of the factorization mechanism and offer valuable input for probing possible physics beyond the Standard Model in forthcoming high-luminosity experiments.
